Guide

Record a doctor’s appointment and keep the notes

Verbi is a voice recorder for iPhone and Android that writes down what it records. Record a doctor’s appointment, with everyone’s permission, and you leave with the whole conversation as text and a short summary of what was said, so you can read it again at home or share it with someone who could not come. It’s free to start, with 60 minutes of transcription a month.

Free to download, with 60 minutes of transcription every month.

Last updated: November 18, 2026

How do I record a doctor’s visit?

  1. Ask before you record. Tell the doctor you would like to record the conversation to remember it, and record only if they agree. The rules on recording differ from country to country.
  2. Open Verbi and tap Record & Transcribe when the conversation starts. Put the phone on the desk between you, screen down if you like.
  3. Tap stop when you leave. Verbi turns the recording into text; a 20-minute visit takes a minute or two.
  4. Read the summary. Choose the Doctor’s Visit template to get it arranged as what was discussed, what was advised, medicines and doses as they were said, and next steps.
  5. Copy the text to keep it, or with Pro share it as a TXT, PDF or Word (DOCX) file with a family member or carer.

What do I get after the visit?

  • The whole conversation as text, with timestamps, so you can find the moment something was said and listen to it again.
  • A summary written to keep to what was said. Medicines, doses and dates are written as they were spoken, and anything unclear in the recording is marked as unclear so you can check it against the prescription.
  • With Pro, each voice kept apart, so you can see what the doctor said and what you asked.
  • Search across all your recordings for a word, such as the name of a medicine.
  • With Pro, answers to questions like “When is the next appointment?”, drawn from the recording itself.

What should I keep in mind?

  • Verbi writes down and summarizes what was said. It does not give medical advice and does not check whether anything said is correct.
  • Speech recognition makes mistakes, and medicine names and numbers are where they matter most. Check anything important against the recording, the written prescription or your doctor.
  • A quiet room and a phone close to both of you give the best text. Add the names of your medicines to Custom Vocabulary in Settings before you go.
  • On the free plan, recordings are kept for 15 days: copy the text you want to keep.

Is it free, and where does the recording go?

You can start free. The free plan includes 60 minutes of transcription and 3 AI summaries a month, with recordings kept for 15 days. You choose the summary template on either plan. Verbi Pro adds hours of transcription, a summary for every recording, speaker detection, chat with the transcript, export to TXT, PDF and Word (DOCX), and history that is not deleted automatically. There is no account to create.

Recordings and transcripts are stored on your phone. To transcribe, the audio is sent to our speech-to-text providers (ElevenLabs and OpenAI), usually through our server, and summaries and chat send the transcript text to OpenAI. The privacy policy lists what is sent and where.

Frequently asked questions

Am I allowed to record my doctor’s appointment?

It depends on where you live and on the practice. Ask first, and record only if the doctor agrees. Verbi shows that it is recording on your screen; it is up to you to tell the people in the room.

Does Verbi understand medical terms?

It transcribes what it hears and gets many medical terms right, but it can misspell names of medicines. Add them to Custom Vocabulary before the visit, and check names and doses against the prescription.

Can I share the notes with my family?

Yes. Copy the text and paste it into a message on any plan, or with Pro share the transcript and summary as a TXT, PDF or Word (DOCX) file.

Can I record an appointment in another language?

Yes. Verbi transcribes 39 languages and detects the language on its own. With Pro, you can translate the transcript into 15 languages.
